paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: you don't live like God's child to become one, you live like one because you ARE one. Paul says, "Be imitators of God, therefore, as beloved children" (Ephesians 5:1). See the order? Loved first, copying second, like a little one clomping around in big shoes, and the big shoes are love, the kind Christ showed when He "gave Himself up for us" (Ephesians 5:2). So nobody's copying to earn a spot, they're copying because they've already got one.

That same truth runs through the whole passage. Paul says "you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord" (Ephesians 5:8). So the walk comes from who you are now, and it grows fruit: "all goodness, righteousness, and truth" (Ephesians 5:9). And light doesn't stay put either, because "everything that is illuminated becomes a light itself" (Ephesians 5:13). If you feel like you're nodding off, hear the wake-up call: "Wake up, O sleeper, rise up from the dead, and Christ will shine on you." (Ephesians 5:14)

So here's what that means for your day, baker. Pay careful attention to how you walk, redeem the time, and understand what the Lord's will is (Ephesians 5:15-17). Be "filled with the Spirit" (Ephesians 5:18), and let that overflow into songs and thanks, "always giving thanks to God the Father for everything" (Ephesians 5:20). Nothing else fills you up like that, and trust me, I've tried to fill up on cookie dough.
